title: ANALYZE, statistics and a planner deciding on stale numbers

videos.script: A report that took eighty milliseconds yesterday takes seven hundred today. Nobody changed the query. Nobody dropped an index. {{yesterday}} What changed is the table. Last night an import added three hundred thousand rows, and the planner has not heard about them. {{import}} The planner never reads the rows to choose a plan. It reads a summary of them: how many rows there are, how many different values each column holds, and which values are common. ANALYZE writes that summary, from a sample. {{summary}} Between a big change and the next ANALYZE, every plan is made on old numbers. You will open that window on purpose, and watch the planner expect one row where there are three hundred thousand. {{one-row}} Then one statement closes it. {{fixed}} After that, the parts that are yours to look after. When autovacuum analyses a table by itself, and why that can be too late. How much of a table the sample reads, and when to make it bigger. {{sample}} And why a database that was just restored, or just upgraded, starts with no summary at all. {{title}}
